judgment.notes: The commutators act on the same complex module and H004 supplies both induction bases. The dimension argument has exactly n independent vectors and dim_C V=n. All factorial divisors and distinct-weight scalar differences are nonzero in C, including when p=2; no characteristic-p calculation is used. The finite-dimensional and binomial background facts have the conditions recorded below. There are no E/M applications.

Both power identities have correct bases and induction steps. Applying x^i proves e_i nonzero; the displayed polynomial in h isolates each coefficient and proves independence. Dimension then gives the basis. Expanding y^(λ+1)v in that basis forces all coefficients to vanish since 2(λ+1-i) is nonzero for i∈I; further powers give every d>λ. Dividing the one-step formulas by the nonzero factorials gives exactly both stated binomial coefficients and both zero cases. Empty products handle λ=0 and r=0. There are no limiting operations.

Only H001–H004, D001/D002/D004–D006, earlier F001–F003, and the recorded routine background are needed. L1 and L2 are discharged induction hypotheses; L3 is discharged after an arbitrary relation and arbitrary j have been treated. The arbitrary indices stay in their declared scopes, and coefficient expansion is justified by the already proved basis. No output or future fact is used as a premise. H001 supplies λ≥0; its prime/field-characteristic clauses and the irreducibility/highest-weight description beyond the explicit dimension in H002 are unused.
